title: The Central Coast
subtitle: Santa Barbara to Monterey
objectives: Explain the transverse valleys of Santa Barbara

steps.title: A long coast
steps.body: The Central Coast runs from San Francisco Bay to Santa Barbara. Monterey's Salinas Valley is cool and windy, good for Chardonnay and Pinot Noir. Paso Robles is warmer, with large day and night swings, making Cabernet Sauvignon, Zinfandel and Rhône grapes, a movement known as the Rhône Rangers.

steps.title: Transverse valleys
steps.body: In Santa Barbara County, the Santa Ynez Valley runs east to west, unusual on the American coast. This lets cold Pacific air flow straight in. The Sta. Rita Hills, near the sea, are cool enough for fine Pinot Noir and Chardonnay; further inland, Happy Canyon is warm enough for Bordeaux grapes.
steps.highlight: East-west valleys bring in the ocean

steps.prompt: Santa Barbara's valleys run east to west, letting ocean air flow inland.
steps.explanation: Yes. That orientation brings cool Pacific air deep into the valleys, making them ideal for Pinot Noir.

steps.body: The film Sideways, set in Santa Barbara County in 2004, made Pinot Noir sales jump in the US, and hurt Merlot's reputation for years.

steps.prompt: Which grapes are associated with the Rhône Rangers in Paso Robles?
steps.explanation: Rhône Rangers grow Rhône grapes like Syrah, Grenache, Mourvèdre and Viognier.

steps.title: What you learned
points: The Central Coast runs from cool Monterey to Santa Barbara
Santa Barbara's east-west valleys let in cool Pacific air
Paso Robles grows Rhône grapes, Zinfandel and Cabernet
